tasks.short: Answer manager and employee questions, explain contract and CAO terms, help sort out conflicts on the floor.

today.trigger: A team leader calls, mails or stops by about an employee issue, a contract clause or a shift dispute.
steps: Listen to the question or complaint and ask what happened
Look up the contract, CAO article or absence history in AFAS
Check earlier mails and notes in Outlook and SharePoint
Talk to the manager and the employee, sometimes together
Agree on next steps and write a short note
drudgery: Searching contract versions and CAO articles
Re-explaining the same rules to different team leaders
today.time_sinks: Context gathering across AFAS, mailboxes and old notes before each conversation, and follow-up notes after it.

lenses.faster: A case brief (contract, CAO scale, absence history, earlier notes) is ready before the call, and a note draft is ready after it.
lenses.autonomous: Routine questions go to the policy agent in Teams first; only personal or disputed cases reach the HRBP, with the brief attached.
lenses.ambitious: Every team leader on all three sites, including night shifts, gets an answer the same day instead of waiting for the HRBP's site day.
lenses.joy: Less searching and retyping; more time in the warehouse with people, which is why most HRBPs took the job.
lenses.options: For a conflict, the copilot sets out two or three ways forward with the CAO and legal limits of each.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP owns the escalation rules and the knowledge base of the front door and reviews which cases keep coming back.
reach: HR Administrator: contract questions and letters
Payroll Specialist: first-line pay slip questions

tasks.human_edge: Trust with shift workers and team leaders, reading the room in a conflict, and judging when an issue is really about something else.
tasks.pattern_why: The person leads the conversation and the outcome; AI prepares case briefs, finds clauses and drafts notes.

in_practice.trigger: A case is opened from a Teams message, a mail, or an escalation from the policy agent.
steps: Copilot pulls contract, CAO scale, absence and earlier notes into a one-page brief
HRBP reads the brief and holds the conversation
Copilot drafts the case note and follow-up mail from the HRBP's bullet points
HRBP edits and files the note in the personnel file
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP decides what is said and agreed, and signs off every note before it is filed.
data_needed: Escalation tickets from the front door
in_practice.logs_to: Case note in the AFAS personnel file; case log on SharePoint with open and closed dates

evidence.claim: IBM's Ask HR handles 11 million interactions a year; about 180 HRBPs act as first human support for escalated complex cases.
evidence.source: Cornell CAHRS HRBP Exchange hosted by IBM, May 2026 [S1]

evidence.claim: Danish HR professionals using chatbots saved about 3% of their hours on average.
Copilot can summarise mail threads and documents a user has access to.

risks: Personal data in briefs needs a DPIA and OR consent (WOR art. 27(1)(k))
Copilot access rights too wide, showing files the HRBP should not see
Notes that read as AI-written reduce trust
research_questions: How many hours per week does each HRBP spend gathering context versus in conversation?
Will IT approve Copilot on AFAS personnel data, or only on mail and SharePoint?
What share of incoming questions are personal cases that cannot go to a bot?

tasks.short: Explain HR policies, CAO rules and laws like verlof, verzuim and overtime to managers and staff.

today.trigger: A question by mail, Teams or phone: holiday hours, overtime pay, sick reporting, notice periods.
steps: Read the question and work out which CAO or policy applies
Look up the article in the CAO or SharePoint policy
Check the person's contract type if relevant
Write or say the answer in plain Dutch
Answer the same question again next week
drudgery: Finding which version of a policy is current
Translating legal text into plain words
today.time_sinks: Repetition: most questions are general and already answered in a policy or the CAO.

lenses.faster: General questions are answered in seconds by an agent quoting the CAO or policy article; the HRBP only sees escalations.
lenses.autonomous: The Teams agent answers 24/7, logs each question and opens a ticket when it is unsure or the question is personal.
lenses.ambitious: Shift workers and flex workers get answers in Dutch, English and Polish at 3 a.m., for the first time.
lenses.joy: No more answering the holiday-hours question for the twentieth time; the HRBP handles the cases that need judgment.
lenses.options: For a grey-area question the agent shows the relevant articles and two readings, and flags it for the HRBP.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP curates the policy content, reviews wrong or escalated answers weekly and fixes the source text.
reach: HR Administrator: standard information requests
Compensation and Benefits Specialist: explaining pay scales and allowances
Payroll Specialist: questions on overtime and shift allowances

tasks.human_edge: Interpreting unclear or conflicting rules, judging a personal situation, and owning the answer when it has legal weight.
tasks.pattern_why: An agent on owned content answers general policy questions; personal or uncertain cases escalate to the HRBP, who handles exceptions.

in_practice.trigger: An employee or manager asks a question in the Teams HR agent.
steps: Agent states it is an AI and answers from SharePoint policies and CAO texts with the article cited
If the question is personal, disputed or low-confidence, it opens a ticket with the conversation attached
HRBP answers the ticket and marks whether the source text needs fixing
Weekly, the HRBP reviews a sample of answers and the top unanswered questions
in_practice.human_gate: Personal cases and anything with legal consequence go to the HRBP; the HRBP approves all changes to the knowledge base.
data_needed: Current CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer and warehouse CAO
in_practice.logs_to: Conversation log and ticket list in a SharePoint list, reviewed monthly in Power BI

evidence.claim: IBM's Ask HR handles over 11 million interactions a year with 40% savings and routes complex cases to HRBPs.
evidence.source: Cornell CAHRS HRBP Exchange hosted by IBM [S1]

evidence.claim: Coca-Cola Andina's HR agent serves 1,200 of 3,600 staff monthly with CSAT 4.1 and opens tickets for unanswered questions.
Employee-facing AI systems must disclose that they are AI.

risks: Wrong answer on pay or notice periods creates a claim
Out-of-date policy on SharePoint gets quoted as current
OR consent needed if the agent reads personnel data (WOR art. 27)
Low use by shift workers without a work laptop
research_questions: What share of the last three months' questions are general versus personal?
Can shift workers reach Teams on their phone, or is another channel needed?
How accurate is the agent on a test set of 100 real questions, checked by an HRBP?
Will the OR consent to a general-content agent without personnel data in phase one?

tasks.short: Match people to teams, shifts and roles across the three sites, and sort out staffing gaps with managers.

today.trigger: A reorganisation, a site that is short-staffed, an internal move request or a peak season.
steps: Get headcount and open roles from AFAS and Power BI
Talk to site managers about skills and gaps
List candidates for moves, including certificates from Studytube
Discuss options with managers and employees
Record the change in AFAS
drudgery: Building the same staffing Excel by hand
Checking who holds forklift, VCA or food safety certificates
today.time_sinks: Combining headcount, contracts and certificates from different systems into one picture.

lenses.faster: A standard staffing view joins AFAS headcount and Studytube certificates per site, so the Excel work disappears.
lenses.autonomous: The view refreshes nightly and flags sites below minimum certified staff for a shift.
lenses.ambitious: Internal moves are offered first, before agencies are called, across all three sites.
lenses.joy: Less spreadsheet building; more time on the conversation about who fits where.
lenses.options: Two or three staffing scenarios (internal move, flex, overtime) with cost and certificate coverage.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP sets the matching rules with site managers and checks the outcomes for fairness.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: staffing dashboards
Recruiter: deciding internal versus external hire

tasks.human_edge: Knowing people and teams, fairness between employees, and the negotiation with managers and the OR.
tasks.pattern_why: Data joining is deterministic; the decision about people stays with the HRBP and managers, and scoring people would be high-risk under the AI Act.

in_practice.trigger: A staffing request or the monthly site review.
steps: Power BI view joins AFAS roles and Studytube certificates per site
Copilot drafts scenarios with cost and coverage
HRBP and site manager choose and talk to the employees
HR Administrator records the change in AFAS
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP and the manager make every placement decision; no automatic ranking of people.
in_practice.logs_to: Decision note in AFAS and a staffing log on SharePoint

evidence.claim: Microsoft's Workforce Insights agent shows managers team structure and staffing without asking HR.
AI that allocates tasks on behaviour or traits is high-risk from 2 December 2027.

risks: A matching score would fall under Annex III high-risk duties
Perceived favouritism if scenarios look automated
Certificate data in Studytube out of date
research_questions: How often per month do placement decisions happen and how long does the data gathering take?
Is Studytube certificate data complete enough to join with AFAS?
Would the OR accept a staffing view at person level, or only at team level?

tasks.short: Advise managers on recruiting and keeping people, like referral schemes, onboarding and retention for warehouse staff.

today.trigger: High turnover at a site, a hard-to-fill role, or the yearly HR plan.
steps: Pull turnover and time-to-hire figures from Power BI and Recruitee
Read exit reasons and talk to team leaders
Look at what other firms do
Write a proposal in PowerPoint
Present it to site management
drudgery: Rebuilding turnover cuts by site and tenure in Excel
Reading exit notes one by one
today.time_sinks: Analysis and slide building before the actual advice conversation.

lenses.faster: Copilot summarises 90-day leavers, exit reasons and Recruitee stage data into a first draft of the problem and options.
lenses.autonomous: A monthly note flags sites where 90-day retention drops below target, with the main exit reasons.
lenses.ambitious: Every site gets its own retention plan reviewed each quarter, instead of one company plan a year.
lenses.joy: Less slide building; more time testing ideas with team leaders.
lenses.options: Three to five program options (buddy system, shift choice, faster start, referral bonus) with expected cost and effect.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP owns the retention measures behind the North Star and checks which programs actually move 90-day retention.
reach: Recruiter: hiring channel analysis
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: retention analysis
L&D Specialist: onboarding program design

tasks.human_edge: Knowing why people leave this site, persuading managers, and judging what fits the CAO and budget.
tasks.pattern_why: The HRBP leads the advice; AI speeds up the analysis and drafts options.

in_practice.trigger: Monthly retention signal or a manager request.
steps: Power BI computes 90-day retention and time to hire per site
Copilot groups exit reasons and drafts a problem summary
Copilot drafts program options with costs
HRBP tests options with the manager and finalises the proposal
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP chooses which options to recommend and presents them.
data_needed: Hires and leavers by site and tenure
in_practice.logs_to: Proposal and decision on SharePoint; outcome tracked in the Power BI retention dashboard

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI and PowerPoint can draft summaries and slides from data.
LLMs can group free-text exit reasons into themes.

risks: Small numbers per site make conclusions shaky
Exit notes contain personal data; aggregate before analysis
Generic best-practice options that do not fit logistics shift work
research_questions: Are exit reasons recorded consistently in AFAS today?
Which past retention programs had a measured effect on 90-day retention?
How many hours does a typical retention proposal take now?

tasks.short: Train team leaders on interviews, appraisals, difficult conversations and documenting poor performance properly.

today.trigger: A new team leader, the appraisal cycle, or a manager with a performance case.
steps: Prepare training material or a one-to-one briefing
Explain the process and the dossier rules for UWV or kantonrechter
Practise a conversation with the manager
Review the manager's written notes
drudgery: Rewriting the same guidance per manager
today.time_sinks: One-to-one coaching repeated per manager, and checking dossier notes.

lenses.faster: Standard modules in Studytube plus a prep copilot for managers cut repeated one-to-one explanations.
lenses.autonomous: Before each appraisal round, managers get a short refresher and a checklist in Teams.
lenses.ambitious: Every team leader, including night shift, can practise a difficult conversation by role-play before having it.
lenses.joy: The HRBP stops repeating the basics and coaches on real, harder cases.
lenses.options: The copilot offers several ways to open a conversation or phrase feedback, and the manager picks.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP designs the manager curriculum and reviews where documentation still fails.
reach: L&D Specialist: manager training modules
Recruiter: interview training for hiring managers

tasks.human_edge: Coaching on real cases, credibility with managers, and judging when a case needs legal care.
tasks.pattern_why: Training and preparation stay human-led; AI drafts material and offers role-play practice.

in_practice.trigger: Appraisal cycle starts or a manager asks for help with a case.
steps: Manager uses a role-play and prep assistant built on Noordhaven guidance
Copilot checks a draft performance note for facts, dates and agreed actions
HRBP reviews the note and coaches on the hard parts
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP reviews any note that goes into a dossier; the manager owns the conversation.
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube completions; final notes in the AFAS personnel file

evidence.claim: IBM pilots role-play for difficult conversations for managers; no outcome data yet.
Workday's check-in agent raised users' share of 'Good' feedback by 16 points against 7 for non-users.
Managers report employees can tell AI-drafted feedback and become more closed off.

risks: Feedback that sounds AI-written damages trust
A note tool that rates performance becomes high-risk from Dec 2027
Managers skip the HRBP on cases that need legal care
research_questions: How many dossier notes failed review last year and why?
Do team leaders use a role-play tool if offered, measured in a pilot at one site?
Does AI-checked documentation hold up better in UWV or kantonrechter procedures?

tasks.short: Set up ways to hear how staff feel about policies and working conditions, including the complaint procedure.

today.trigger: Yearly survey planning, a CAO change, an OR request or a rise in complaints.
steps: Decide what to measure with the HR Director and OR
Design or adapt a survey and pulse questions
Review and update the complaint procedure
Agree on anonymity and data use with the OR
today.time_sinks: Alignment rounds with the OR and management on design and privacy.

lenses.faster: Copilot drafts question sets, complaint flow options and a DPIA outline from Noordhaven's policies.
lenses.autonomous: Short pulse surveys run after set events (first week, day 90, shift change) without a manual reminder.
lenses.ambitious: Listening happens at site and shift level all year, and results feed the 90-day retention measure.
lenses.joy: Less drafting from zero; more time agreeing with the OR on what matters.
lenses.options: Several survey designs and complaint routes with their privacy and cost trade-offs.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP owns the listening system design and its rules on anonymity and follow-up.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: survey design
HR Director: OR consultation preparation

tasks.human_edge: Agreement with the OR, judging what is fair monitoring, and building trust that complaints are safe.
tasks.pattern_why: Design choices involve the OR, privacy and trust; AI drafts and compares options.

in_practice.trigger: Survey cycle or change in the complaint procedure.
steps: Copilot drafts question sets and complaint flow options
HRBP selects and adapts with the HR Director
OR reviews under its consent right
Event-based pulses are set up in Forms and Power Automate
in_practice.human_gate: OR consent and HR Director approval before any new monitoring method goes live.
in_practice.logs_to: Design decisions and OR advice on SharePoint

evidence.claim: Emotion inference from face or voice at work is banned.
Works council consent is needed for systems that can observe behaviour or performance.
People affected by an AI outcome must be able to complain.

risks: Text sentiment on Teams messages counts as monitoring and needs consent
Survey fatigue among shift workers
Small teams make anonymous results traceable
research_questions: What response rates do shift workers give on phone surveys today?
Will the OR consent to event-based pulse surveys?
How many complaints came in last year and how were they handled?

tasks.short: Make reports and slides on employee satisfaction and survey results for site and company management.

today.trigger: Survey closes or quarterly management meeting.
steps: Export survey data to Excel
Make charts by site and department
Read open comments and pick themes
Build the PowerPoint and present it
today.time_sinks: Reading and coding open comments, and building slides.

lenses.faster: Charts are a fixed Power BI dashboard; an LLM step groups comments into themes with example quotes.
lenses.autonomous: When a survey closes the dashboard refreshes and a draft summary is ready the next morning.
lenses.ambitious: Each site and shift gets its own short report with actions, not one company deck a year.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses coding comments in Excel; the HRBP spends time on what to do about them.
lenses.options: Draft summaries for different audiences: management team, site manager, OR.
lenses.altitude: The HRBP checks theme quality and owns the follow-up actions, not the slide building.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: survey reporting
HR Director: OR reporting

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what the results mean, which messages to bring, and presenting hard news to management.
tasks.pattern_why: Charts are deterministic; turning open comments into themes is an LLM step inside a fixed workflow that a person checks.

steps: Power BI refreshes scores by site and team (minimum group size enforced)
LLM step groups comments into themes with counts and quotes, removing names
HRBP checks themes against a sample of raw comments
Copilot drafts the deck; HRBP edits and presents
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP approves themes and the deck before anyone else sees it.
in_practice.logs_to: Report and theme coding on SharePoint; dashboard in Power BI

evidence.claim: Power BI dashboards refresh automatically on new data; Copilot drafts summaries and slides.
LLMs reliably group free-text survey comments into themes when checked by a person.

risks: Themes miss rare but serious complaints
Small groups identifiable, breaching AVG
Quotes that reveal who wrote them
research_questions: How close are LLM themes to an HRBP's own coding on last year's survey?
What minimum group size will the OR accept for reporting?
How many hours did last year's report take?

role.altitude: The HRBP moves from answering questions to running the HR front door: owning the policy agent's content and escalation rules, the manager toolkit and the retention measures, acting as second line for complex cases, possibly in pods by function as at IBM.
reach: HR Administrator: standard information requests and contract letters
Payroll Specialist: first-line pay and allowance questions
L&D Specialist: manager training modules
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: survey and retention reporting
Recruiter: retention analysis and interview training for hiring managers
role.ceiling_note: Across these seven tasks (about 800 hours per FTE a year) roughly 280 hours per FTE could be freed, about 17% of the year, or some EUR 22,000 per FTE. Limits: conflict handling, trust and legal ownership stay human; OR consent and AVG decide data access; tools that score or allocate people become high-risk under the AI Act from December 2027.
skills_to_grow: Writing and maintaining a policy knowledge base for an agent
Setting escalation rules and reviewing agent answers
Basic Power BI and data literacy
AI Act, AVG and WOR art. 27 compliance for HR tools
Coaching managers to use AI prep without losing their own voice
role.ambitious_version: Every team leader and shift worker on all three sites gets a correct policy answer within minutes in their own language, every manager practises hard conversations before having them, and each site has a quarterly retention plan tied to 90-day retention, with three HRBPs spending most of their time on the floor.
